newsitem.title: USA: FTC moves to block Mediq-Universal Hospital merger.
newsitem.headline: FTC moves to block Mediq-Universal Hospital merger.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission said Tuesday it will ask a judge to block a proposed $100 million merger of the nation's largest companies renting medical equipment: Mediq Inc. and Universal Hospital Services Inc.
The FTC will argue in court that if the merger goes through, Mediq will be able to raise prices above competitive levels.

"The result will be higher rental prices because hospitals and hospital chains will not switch from renting to buying expensive equipment that may sit idle for long periods, even in the face of a significant rental price increase," the FTC said.
The FTC, which voted 5-0 against the deal, will challenge the merger in U.S. District Court.
In February, Mediq announced its plan to acquire Universal for $17.50 a share.
Both companies rent durable, movable medical equipment that can be delivered to hospitals during peak need periods, the FTC said.
Mediq, based in Pennsauken, N.J., has 85 rental facilities and more than 130,000 pieces of equipment. Universal, of Bloomington, Minn., has 46 rental facilities and 40,000 pieces of equipment.
The FTC said other companies renting such equipment are local or regional, are much smaller or rent only a limited line of equipment.
The FTC will seek a preliminary injunction in court. When the FTC has sought and won preliminary injunctions in the past, they have usually had the effect of killing mergers.
Mediq's stock price slipped 62.5 cents to $7.375 in afternoon trading on the American Stock Exchange. Universal fell $1.50 to $11.375 on Nasdaq.
